transcript:
Doctor: What brought you in?
Patient: I have a headache.
Doctor: How long has it been there?
Patient: Three days.
Doctor: How bad is it?
Patient: Mild.
Doctor: Have you taken anything for it?
Patient: I took ibuprofen this morning.
Doctor: Any medication allergies?
Patient: I'm allergic to penicillin.

Doctor: Tell me about the problem today.
Patient: A cough is bothering me.
Doctor: When did the cough start?
Patient: One week ago.
Doctor: Would you call it mild, moderate, or severe?
Patient: Moderate.
Doctor: What have you used for it so far?
Patient: Nothing. I haven't taken any medicine for it.
Doctor: Do you have any drug allergies?
Patient: No medication allergies.

Doctor: What's the main reason for this visit?
Patient: My throat is sore.
Doctor: For how many days?
Patient: Two days now.
Doctor: How would you describe the severity?
Patient: It's severe.

Doctor: Where are you having trouble?
Patient: My lower back hurts.
Doctor: How intense is that pain?
Patient: Mild, really.
Doctor: Have you tried a medicine for the back pain?
Patient: No, I haven't tried any.
Doctor: Are you allergic to any medications?
Patient: Penicillin.

Doctor: What's troubling you?
Patient: I've got a headache.
Doctor: When did it begin, and how strong is it?
Patient: It began yesterday. It's moderate.
Doctor: Did you take anything for the headache?
Patient: I may have, but I honestly can't remember whether I took a tablet or just got the packet out.
Doctor: Can you be certain either way?
Patient: No, I can't say.
Doctor: Any allergies to medicines?
Patient: None that I know of.

Doctor: Tell me what hurts.
Patient: My throat. It's been sore for four days.
Doctor: How bad does it feel?
Patient: Mild.
Doctor: Have you used anything from the medicine cabinet?
Patient: I haven't taken so much as a lozenge or a pill for this.
Doctor: And your medication allergies?
Patient: I'm allergic to penicillin.

Doctor: What are we discussing today?
Patient: A headache that started two days ago.
Doctor: How severe is the headache?
Patient: Moderate.
Doctor: What have you taken for it?
Patient: One capsule from my travel pouch, but I can't tell you what it was called.
Doctor: Do you remember the name on the packet?
Patient: There wasn't a packet in the pouch. I don't know the name.
Doctor: Any medication allergies?
Patient: No, none.

Doctor: What symptom is bothering you most?
Patient: A sore throat, since yesterday morning.
Doctor: Is it mild, moderate, or severe?
Patient: Moderate.
Doctor: Have you tried ibuprofen or anything else?
Patient: I thought about taking ibuprofen and bought some, but the box is still unopened. I haven't used any medicine for this.
Doctor: Any drugs you are allergic to?
Patient: No medication allergies.

Doctor: Why have you come in?
Patient: I've had a mild headache for three days.
Doctor: What did you take for it?
Patient: Ibuprofen last night.
Doctor: Have you taken anything else?
Patient: I haven't taken any medicine at all for this headache.
Doctor: Earlier you said ibuprofen last night. Which account should I use?
Patient: I'm mixing things up, and I can't settle which is right.
Doctor: Any medication allergies?
Patient: Penicillin.

Doctor: What's the problem today?
Patient: My lower back has hurt for six days.
Doctor: How severe is it?
Patient: Moderate.
Doctor: What have you tried for the pain?
Patient: Acetaminophen on Monday and ibuprofen on Tuesday.
Doctor: Were those both for this back pain?
Patient: Yes, both of them were for this same episode.
Doctor: Any medication allergies?
Patient: I don't have any.

Doctor: What brought you here?
Patient: A moderate headache that's lasted four days.
Doctor: Which medicine have you tried for it?
Patient: Aspirin.
Doctor: When did you take the aspirin?
Patient: Sorry, that was for a headache months ago. For this one I took ibuprofen yesterday, not aspirin.
Doctor: Did you take any other medicine for the current headache?
Patient: No, just the ibuprofen.
Doctor: Do you have any medication allergies?
Patient: Penicillin.

Doctor: What's been bothering you?
Patient: A sore throat for two days.
Doctor: How bad is the soreness?
Patient: Mild.
Doctor: Any medicine tried for this?
Patient: Nothing yet.
Doctor: You mentioned a tablet earlier. Was that for this throat?
Patient: Yes. I was describing how things were before yesterday. I took acetaminophen last night for the throat.
Doctor: Any other medicine for it since then?
Patient: No, that was the only one.
Doctor: Any drug allergies?
Patient: None.

Doctor: What would you like to discuss?
Patient: I've had a headache for five days.
Doctor: How intense is it?
Patient: Moderate.
Doctor: Have you tried any medication?
Patient: I took ibuprofen yesterday.
Doctor: Are you allergic to any medicines?
Patient: I'm not sure about penicillin. Someone once said I had a rash as a child, but I don't know whether it was an allergy.
Doctor: Has that ever been confirmed?
Patient: No, I don't know that it has.

Doctor: What is the main complaint?
Patient: A mild cough for three days.
Doctor: Have you taken a medicine for it?
Patient: No medicine for the cough.
Doctor: The intake question mentions penicillin. Is that an allergy you have?
Patient: No, I'm not allergic to penicillin. I have no medication allergies.
Doctor: Is there another symptom you want to discuss?
Patient: No, just the cough.

Doctor: Tell me about today's symptom.
Patient: A sore throat. It started two days ago and feels moderate.
Doctor: What have you taken for it?
Patient: Acetaminophen this morning.
Doctor: Which medicines are you allergic to?
Patient: Penicillin and sulfa antibiotics.
Doctor: Are you naming two separate allergies?
Patient: Yes. Both are allergies I have been told I have.

Doctor: What's the concern today?
Patient: A headache for one week. It's mild.
Doctor: Any medication tried for it?
Patient: Ibuprofen.
Doctor: Any medication allergies?
Patient: There is one, but I can't remember whether the name was penicillin or a sulfa antibiotic.
Doctor: Can you identify it more precisely?
Patient: No. I don't have the old card, and I would be guessing.

Doctor: What is bothering you?
Patient: A headache.
Doctor: How long have you had it?
Patient: Since that stretch when everything was happening. I can't place it on a day or say how long ago.
Doctor: How bad is the headache?
Patient: Moderate.
Doctor: Have you tried any medicine for it?
Patient: Ibuprofen yesterday.
Doctor: What medication allergies do you have?
Patient: Penicillin.

Doctor: What symptom are you here for?
Patient: My throat has been sore for three days.
Doctor: How would you rate the severity?
Patient: It's somewhere between a nuisance and a real problem. I can't choose mild, moderate, or severe.
Doctor: What medicine have you tried?
Patient: Acetaminophen last night.
Doctor: Any medication allergies?
Patient: No medication allergies.

Doctor: How was the bus ride over?
Patient: Quiet. I watched the rain on the window.
Doctor: What brings you in today?
Patient: A cough.
Doctor: How long have you had it?
Patient: Four days.
Doctor: How bad would you say it is?
Patient: Mild.
Doctor: Have you tried any medicine for the cough?
Patient: Nothing at all.
Doctor: Any medication allergies?
Patient: I'm allergic to penicillin.

Doctor: What has been hurting?
Patient: My lower back for five days.
Doctor: What level of pain is it?
Patient: Moderate.
Doctor: Have you taken anything for it?
Patient: A little green tablet from a packet I no longer have. I don't know its name.
Doctor: Can you tell me anything else about that tablet?
Patient: No, that's all I remember about it.
Doctor: Any medication allergies?
Patient: Penicillin.

Doctor: What's the main reason you're here?
Patient: The headache. I've also had a cough, but the headache is what I want to discuss.
Doctor: How long has each been going on?
Patient: The headache started three days ago. The cough started a week ago.
Doctor: How severe is the headache?
Patient: Moderate. The cough is only mild.
Doctor: Any medicine tried for the headache?
Patient: No, nothing for the headache.
Doctor: Do you have any medication allergies?
Patient: Penicillin.

Doctor: What is troubling you?
Patient: I've had a headache for two days.
Doctor: You look uncomfortable; I'll describe the headache as severe.
Patient: Could I open the window a little?
Doctor: Have you taken a medicine for the headache?
Patient: I took ibuprofen last night.
Doctor: Do you have any medication allergies?
Patient: No medication allergies.

Doctor: Tell me what's brought you in.
Patient: It's a headache. I was hoping it would pass, and I kept putting the visit off, but the headache is the reason I'm here.
Doctor: When did this episode start?
Patient: Four days ago. I remember because it began while I was tidying the kitchen, then it was still there when I sat down that evening.
Doctor: How would you describe its severity?
Patient: Moderate is the best word. I notice it throughout the day, but I wouldn't call it severe, and mild doesn't really describe it either.
Doctor: What have you tried for it?
Patient: I took ibuprofen yesterday. I had to look around for the packet first, but that is definitely the medicine I used for this headache.
Doctor: Any medication allergies?
Patient: No. I've been asked that a few times, and I don't have any known medication allergies.

Doctor: What would you like us to focus on?
Patient: This headache. My back used to bother me, but that isn't the problem now.
Doctor: When did it begin?
Patient: Two days ago.
Doctor: How bad is it?
Patient: Mild.
Doctor: Have you tried ibuprofen for it?
Patient: Yes, I took it last night.
Doctor: Are you allergic to penicillin?
Patient: Yes, I am. That is my only medication allergy.
